title: A Regiment for the Uniform
premise: In 1890s coastal Norway, Hazel Eriksen, a mapmaker's apprentice, is secretly completing the master atlas her mentor died for when a stranger named Torvald arrives bearing letters in the dead man's unmistakable hand — proof he lives and that his death was staged to escape the cartographic guild's corrupt directorate. Together they follow the atlas's coded marginalia toward the hidden survey plates that could expose the guild's falsified charts, which have wrecked ships and buried deaths. Hunted by the directorate's enforcers as the workshop is burned around them, Hazel must choose between preserving her quiet life and publishing truth outside any court. The novel ends with the atlas finished and smuggled to print under found-family protection, the directorate disgraced by sailors' testimony, and Hazel signing the work with both her name and her dead master's.
about_author: Emrys Kavanagh is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent years cataloguing damaged nautical charts in northern European collections. They write historical fiction about people whose careful hands hold dangerous truths.

chapters.title: The Weight of Blank Paper
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She works late finishing the dead master Aldric's atlas, hiding her authorship from the guild inspector who visits the workshop. Emotional beat: grief disciplined into routine, and the first hint she is being watched.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Tide Gate
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Torvald arrives soaked from the ferry, carrying three letters in Aldric's handwriting — dated after his funeral. He claims Aldric sent him to find 'the one who finishes it.' Beat: disbelief curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Handwriting of the Drowned
chapters.summary: Torvald's POV. He explains he was Aldric's courier and confesses the death was staged; the guild directorate falsified coastal charts and let ships break for insurance money. Beat: reluctant alliance sealed over candlelight and evidence.

chapters.title: Marginalia
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Deciphering Aldric's coded margin notes in the atlas draft, she finds coordinates pointing to hidden survey plates stored off-site. Beat: wonder — the atlas itself is the map to its own vindication.

chapters.title: The Inspector Returns
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Guild inspector Voss demands the unfinished atlas for 'archiving,' clearly intending to seize or destroy it. Hazel stalls with forged inventory pages. Beat: the low profile is over; she lies well and hates it.

chapters.title: What the Workshop Keeps
chapters.summary: Torvald's POV. Exploring the workshop's back rooms, he discovers Aldric's hidden correspondence with widows of shipwrecked crews — the human cost list. Beat: justice becomes personal, not abstract.

chapters.title: Apprentices and Accomplices
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She quietly recruits fellow apprentices Signe and Bram, testing loyalty with small errands. The workshop becomes a conspiracy of ink-stained hands. Beat: found family forming under pressure.

chapters.title: The Plate Room at Skarvholm
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A storm-delayed expedition to the island archive where the true survey plates are kept; they retrieve two plates but trip an alarm set by Voss's agents. Beat: first blood — a chase across black rocks.

chapters.title: Salt and Ashes
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. They return to find the workshop partially burned, 'accidental.' Three years of reference work gone; only the atlas draft survives because Hazel carried it home. Beat: rage and resolve hardening together.

chapters.title: The Director's Invitation
chapters.summary: Torvald's POV. Director Halvard Rask offers Hazel a commission and Torvald amnesty — if the atlas is delivered uncorrected. The offer reveals how much they know. Beat: temptation framed as mercy, refused.

chapters.title: Signe's Testimony
chapters.summary: Signe's POV. Her father died on the Meridian, wrecked by a falsified chart; she matches the plate discrepancies to the wreck report. Beat: grief converted into evidence, the stakes made flesh.

chapters.title: The Third Plate
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The final plate is held in Rask's private residence. Bram proposes using the guild's own delivery routes against them. Beat: audacity — thieves planning with a librarian's precision.

chapters.title: Night Work
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The infiltration of Rask's house succeeds until Torvald is recognized and captured covering their escape. Beat: victory laced with guilt; the family pays its first price.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Torvald's POV. In custody, Torvald stalls Voss with half-truths while memorizing the layout of the guild strongroom where he'll be held. Beat: endurance as resistance.

chapters.title: The Atlas Must Be Finished
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. With days before the guild's charter review, Hazel completes the final sheets alone, Aldric's voice alive in every annotation. Beat: the apprentice becomes the master mid-sentence.

chapters.title: Voss's Bargain
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Voss privately admits he suspects Rask but fears ruin; Hazel offers him the one thing he wants — to be on the right side of history, documented. Beat: an enemy flipped by ambition and shame.

chapters.title: Breaking the Strongroom
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Using Voss's access and Torvald's memorized layout, they free Torvald and copy the directorate's ledgers during the charter review chaos. Beat: the climax begins — everything risked at once.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Charts
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Before the assembled guild, Hazel presents the corrected atlas and the ledgers; surviving sailors testify. Rask's counterattack collapses when Voss corroborates. Beat: catharsis — justice spoken aloud, outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Ink
chapters.summary: Torvald's POV. Rask flees and is taken at the harbor; the guild dissolves the directorate. Torvald, offered reinstatement, chooses instead to stay with the workshop. Beat: exhaustion, tenderness, chosen belonging.

chapters.title: Two Names on the Cover
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. At the printer's, Hazel inscribes the atlas with both Aldric's name and her own — the first time she has claimed her work publicly. Beat: grief finally given a place to rest.

chapters.title: The New Survey
chapters.summary: Signe's POV. The reformed guild commissions honest charts; Signe, Bram, Torvald, and Hazel take on the spring survey together, the workshop rebuilt. Beat: hope as a working plan, not a wish.

chapters.title: A Regiment for the Uniform
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, coda. Years later, Hazel teaches apprentices the margin-code, telling them maps are promises kept to strangers. On the shelf sits the atlas, spine worn from use. Beat: memory honored by continuation; the found family endures.
